title: WHAT COULD MY SUBSCRIPTION BUSINESS LOOK LIKE?
content:
The easiest way to choose a subscription direction is to stop thinking about the billing schedule and ask what the customer continues receiving.

They might keep access to a software tool. They might receive new content. They might remain part of a membership or community. Or they might continue receiving support, coaching, guidance, or accountability.

The recurring payment only makes sense if the continuing value does.

SOFTWARE OR TOOL
The customer keeps paying for continued use of functionality.

CONTENT
New material keeps arriving or continued access to an evolving body of material remains useful.

MEMBERSHIP OR COMMUNITY
Value may come from participation, relationships, resources, events, accountability, networking, or member benefits.

ONGOING SUPPORT OR COACHING
The customer continues receiving help, feedback, expertise, accountability, or guidance.

If the idea overlaps categories, choose the branch that best describes the reason the customer would continue paying. Other pieces can be added later.

OPTIONS
SOFTWARE / TOOL
Customer keeps paying for continued access to useful functionality.

CONTENT
Customer keeps paying for new/ongoing content.

MEMBERSHIP / COMMUNITY
Customer keeps paying for access to people, community, resources, events, environment,
or member benefits.

ONGOING SUPPORT / COACHING
Customer keeps paying for continuing access to help, guidance, accountability, or
expert support.

POSSIBLE DISTINCT RESOURCE/LIBRARY MODEL
Retain only if development shows it provides a genuinely different decision from
content or membership.

CONTINUING-VALUE TEST
Finish this sentence:
"My customer keeps paying because each month they continue to receive or access ______."

If the honest answer is "because they still owe me for the thing they already bought," you have a payment plan.
If the answer is "because they need another unit of the thing they used up," investigate consumables.
If the blank contains continuing access, functionality, content, community, support, or another ongoing value, the subscription branch is likely useful.

CONTINUED ACCESS TO SOFTWARE OR A TOOL → PDF 33.
CONTINUING CONTENT → PDF 34.
MEMBERSHIP OR COMMUNITY → PDF 35.
ONGOING SUPPORT OR COACHING → PDF 36.
I'D RATHER EARN FROM SOMEONE ELSE'S SUBSCRIPTION → PDF 37.

A SUBSCRIPTION NEEDS A REASON TO SURVIVE THE NEXT BILL
It is easy to imagine why someone would join. Spend equal time imagining the moment before the second, sixth, or twelfth payment.

What would make the customer say, "Yes, I still want this"?

That answer is often more useful than the feature list because it identifies the continuing value the business must actually maintain.

FOUR DIFFERENT REASONS TO KEEP PAYING

SOFTWARE OR TOOL
The customer keeps paying because the functionality remains useful. The important question is what recurring job the tool performs. A tool that is useful once may be better sold as a one-off product.

CONTENT
The customer keeps paying because the content continues to arrive or because continued access to a changing or valuable library matters. If the useful material can be completed once and remain complete, a one-off product may fit better.

MEMBERSHIP OR COMMUNITY
The customer keeps paying because access to the group, interaction, shared activity, resources, accountability, or network continues to matter. The value cannot depend entirely on the promise that a community might become useful later.

ONGOING SUPPORT OR COACHING
The customer keeps paying because continued access to guidance or help has value. This can overlap with services. If the business mainly consists of repeatedly performing tasks for individual customers, the service branch may describe it more accurately.

A resource library does not need a fifth branch of its own. Ask why the customer keeps paying for the library. If the answer is ongoing content, follow content. If the answer is access to a member environment and its resources, follow membership.

ONE IDEA CAN CHANGE CATEGORIES DEPENDING ON THE PROMISE

Imagine a library of meal plans.

Version one is a downloadable collection of 100 meal plans. The customer pays once and keeps the collection. That is naturally a one-off digital product.

Version two adds new plans every week and keeps the full evolving library available only while the customer remains subscribed. Continued content is now part of the value, so a content subscription may fit.

Version three includes the library inside a member community where customers also participate in challenges, discussions, accountability, and live events. The ongoing member environment may now be the stronger reason to stay, making the membership branch more useful.

Version four includes monthly individual calls where someone reviews the customer's situation and gives ongoing guidance. Now the model begins overlapping with ongoing support, coaching, or service.

The subject matter did not determine the model. The continuing promise did.

IF YOUR SUBSCRIPTION COULD FIT TWO CATEGORIES

Choose the reason the customer keeps paying.

If they stay because the TOOL keeps doing a job, start with software/tool.

If they stay because NEW OR CONTINUING MATERIAL remains valuable, start with content.

If they stay because BELONGING, PARTICIPATION, OR ACCESS TO OTHER PEOPLE is central, start with membership/community.

If they stay because ACCESS TO YOUR GUIDANCE OR FEEDBACK remains valuable, start with ongoing support/coaching.

A real offer can contain all four. This question identifies the engine underneath it so you investigate the right risks first.

THE DECISION

Classify the subscription by its main continuing value: repeated functionality, ongoing content, belonging and participation, or ongoing guidance. Mixed offers are normal. Choose the engine underneath the offer and explore that branch first.

WHERE TO GO NEXT
Choose the branch that best explains why the customer keeps paying: PDF 33 software/tool, PDF 34 content, PDF 35 membership/community, or PDF 36 ongoing support/coaching. Use PDF 37 if you want to earn from someone else's subscription instead.
